title: session-cache thrashing causing cross-tenant GPU OOMs and allocator retention
creator: Lena Chen
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments observed intermittent GPU OOMs during prolonged, bursty chat sessions. Investigation shows the session-level cache (session->prefetch index) degenerating into high tombstone density and pointer-churn; the allocator retained large arenas that were never reclaimed due to a corner-case in the free path when tombstones overlapped active KV handles. This led to long-tail memory growth, GPU page thrashing and eventual OOMs under multi-tenant pressure.
steps_taken: Reproduced locally with long-lived session workload (1000+ tokens, intermittent bursts) and tenant mix to emulate hosted noisy neighbors
Added additional tracing for KV handle lifecycle and allocator free events; correlated trace IDs with GPU memory accounting to identify retention windows
Scoped regression range to runtime release 1.18->1.20 where index compaction heuristics changed
Applied temporary routing policy to divert affected customers to cheaper model variants and reduced max concurrency for impacted Dedicated pools
Rolled emergency script to drain and restart 12 hot nodes which cleared immediate OOM incidents for hosted customers
root_cause_analysis: A change to index compaction heuristics coupled with an optimization in the allocator free path created a race where 'tombstoned' KV entries could be re-referenced by in-flight sessions. The allocator's arena refcount logic failed to see the transient return-to-active state, leaving arenas marked in-use and preventing normal reclamation. Over time, tombstone accumulation plus delayed KV sweep triggered GPU page saturation and LRU thrashing, producing OOMs for co-located tenants. The issue is not a single memory leak but allocator retention driven by index fragmentation and handle reuse races under high concurrency.
mitigation_plan: Hotfix patch (runtime-1.21.0-rc1): strengthen free-path atomicity and add a defensive check that forces synchronous tombstone-to-sweep transition when arena pressure is high
Short-term backstop: enable aggressive tombstone compaction flag in runtime config for Hosted and Dedicated (config rollout automated via console)
Traffic-level mitigation: implement per-tenant soft caps and conservative prefetch limits until compaction rollouts complete
Observability: new alerting rule for 'allocator-retained-bytes' and KV tombstone ratio > 0.15 to trigger early mitigation runbooks
follow_up_tasks: ENG-78210: implement background incremental index compactor that is aware of active handle windows
ENG-78305: add unit+stress tests that simulate tombstone reactivation under concurrent session operations
PM-412: customer communications and post-incident report for top 3 impacted accounts
DES-118: console UI flag for 'aggressive compaction' with rollout guardrails
OPS-67: create automatic node-drain playbook to gracefully migrate sessions off high-retention nodes
